blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
People often say 'the UK' and 'England' as if they were the same. They are not. The United Kingdom is four nations: England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland. Each one has its own accent, culture and sometimes its own laws.

A Scottish colleague may sound very different from a Londoner. A Welsh office may feel different from one in Birmingham. These differences are friendly, but they are real — and Brits notice when you ignore them.

Learn the four nations, and you will already seem more attentive.

items.q: How many nations are in the United Kingdom?
items.why: "The United Kingdom is four nations: England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland."

items.q: What does each nation have?
items.why: "Each one has its own accent, culture and sometimes its own laws."

items.q: The text says the differences are…
items.why: "These differences are friendly, but they are real."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with…
options: "The UK and England mean the same thing."
items.why: Inferência: o texto começa dizendo que UK e England NÃO são a mesma coisa.

items.q: "Brits notice when you ignore them" suggests that…
options: England is the only real nation
you should learn the nations to look respectful
items.why: Inferência: se eles percebem, conhecer as nações mostra atenção e respeito.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry falando com um colega. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hey, can I show you something small before you send that email? You wrote 'our English client', but Andrew is not English. He is Scottish. He lives in Edinburgh, and Edinburgh is in Scotland, not England.

I know it feels like a small thing. But for many British people, it is not small. Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland are all part of the United Kingdom, but they are not England. Each one is its own nation, with its own accent and its own culture.

Andrew is very friendly, so he will not shout at you. But he will notice. And if you get it right, he will feel that you pay attention. That is good for the relationship.

So, easy fix: just change 'English' to 'Scottish', or write 'our client in Edinburgh'. Both are safe. Remember, the UK has four nations: England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland. They are one state, but four identities.

Next time you are not sure, ask me, and we will check the city together. It takes ten seconds, and it shows the client that we care about the small things.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What mistake did the colleague make in the email?
options: He sent it to the wrong person
items.why: "You wrote 'our English client', but Andrew is not English. He is Scottish."

items.q: Where does Andrew live?
items.why: "He lives in Edinburgh, and Edinburgh is in Scotland."

items.q: What easy fix does Harry suggest?
items.why: "Just change 'English' to 'Scottish', or write 'our client in Edinburgh'."

items.q: Why does Harry say the mistake is 'not small'?
options: Because it costs a lot of money
Because the nations matter to British people
Because the email is very long
items.why: Inferência: Harry explica que as nações são identidades reais e que Andrew vai perceber.

items.q: How would you describe Harry's tone?
items.why: Inferência: ele corrige com cuidado, dá uma solução fácil e se oferece para ajudar.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Scotland is one nation in the UK." A nation is…
options: a country or people with its own identity
items.why: Nation = nação: um povo ou país com identidade própria.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "His Scottish ___ is strong, so some words are hard to understand."
items.why: Accent = sotaque: o jeito de pronunciar as palavras.

items.q: "Each nation has its own culture." Culture means…
options: the way of life and traditions of a people
items.why: Culture = cultura: o modo de vida e as tradições de um povo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Some ___ are different in Scotland and England, so a rule can change."
items.why: Law = lei; algumas leis mudam de uma nação para outra.

items.q: "Please do not ignore these differences." To ignore means to…
options: not notice or not care about
items.why: To ignore = ignorar: não notar ou não dar atenção.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem no trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Can you point out the mistake in my email?" To point out means to…
items.why: Point out = apontar, mostrar algo para a pessoa ver.

items.q: "It is an easy fix — just change one word." A fix is…
items.why: Fix = correção, uma solução simples para o problema.

items.q: "Let's double-check the city before we send it." To double-check means to…
items.why: Double-check = conferir de novo para ter certeza.

items.q: "He will pick up on the mistake, even if he says nothing." To pick up on means to…
items.why: Pick up on = perceber, notar algo (mesmo sem falar).

items.q: "Getting the name right helps you build up a good relationship." To build up means to…
options: grow or develop step by step
items.why: Build up = construir aos poucos, desenvolver com o tempo.
